analysis.title: The Trump Trend, Anthropic ARR and Alcohol (Top 15 charts)
key_insights: Trump's approval ratings keep sliding. Nate Silver notes the decline has been persistent, with mean reversion around news events and economic data but toward a declining baseline rather than the steady one seen in the first term.

Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate (per TickerTrends) went from roughly $10B in January to $74B by July 24, then to $76.8B on September 24. That is barely 4% growth over two months after a more than sevenfold rise in the first seven months. Revenue has not peaked but the growth trajectory has changed sharply.
The share of US adults who say they drink alcohol fell to 54%, the lowest since Gallup began asking almost 90 years ago, down from the mid-60s a few years back.

CCC-rated spreads have pushed above 1,000bps, and the ratio of CCC spreads to the broader high-yield market is at a record high (MS). Credit stress is concentrating at the bottom of the quality spectrum.
Oracle's five-year CDS has surged to roughly 261bps, near record highs. With a 40% recovery assumption, that implies about 20% cumulative risk-neutral default probability over five years (Bloomberg).
France and NVDA credit default swaps trade at roughly the same level (Marquee), despite one being a sovereign with taxing power and the other an AI chip maker.
US banks are the most oversold versus the overall market since 1993 (Morgan Stanley).
Taiwan and Korea now account for half of the MXAPJ index weight, displacing China as the dominant market (FactSet).
The largest Korean retail broker is down 65% since May after a 'four-bagger' run of about 400% (Flow Show).
EM equities are starting to outperform US equities (BofA).
The ratio of equal-weight S&P 500 (RSP) to market-cap-weight (SPY) has never been lower (Koyfin).
United Wholesale Mortgage, the largest US mortgage lender, hit its lowest closing price in history and is on track for a 9th consecutive red month, its longest losing streak (@barchart).
Share buyback authorizations have reached $1.1 trillion YTD, running more than 20% ahead of last year's pace (GIR).

Hedge fund long/short ratio is at the lowest level of the past year, at the 0th percentile, one of the most extreme positioning readings of 2026 (GS Prime). It could be a warning sign or the setup for the next squeeze.
risk_factors: Credit stress concentrated in the weakest borrowers, with CCC spreads above 1,000bps and a record CCC-to-high-yield spread ratio.
Oracle's five-year CDS near record highs at roughly 261bps.
Slowing AI revenue growth, as seen in Anthropic's run-rate growth of about 4% over two months.
Extreme equity positioning, with the hedge fund long/short ratio at the 0th percentile of the past year.
Record narrow market breadth, with the RSP/SPY ratio at an all-time low.
Weakness in housing finance, with United Wholesale Mortgage at a record low close.
